findings.quote: then poured into a 0.2 M solution of NaOH (30 mL) and Et2O (50 mL)
findings.message: The steps place the transfer before the receiving liquids and omit its source and destination. The source describes pouring the reaction mixture into those liquids, not adding them afterward. The existing uncertainty acknowledges this but does not resolve the operational ordering.

findings.quote: The aqueous and organic layers were partitioned and the aqueous layer was extracted with Et2O (2 x 25 mL). The combined organic extracts
findings.message: The extraction separations leave the retained phase unknown, although the organic extracts are explicitly collected. The aqueous phase must also remain available for the second extraction.
The initial peroxide reagent is identified only as H2O2 in the operational fields. Its specified aqueous formulation should be preserved so that 0.31 mL is not interpreted as neat peroxide.

patch.value: “The aqueous and organic layers were partitioned and the aqueous layer was extracted with Et2O (2 x 25 mL).” Both initial phases must be retained: the initial organic layer joins the organic extracts, while the aqueous layer undergoes two successive extractions. Retain the aqueous raffinate after the first extraction for the second; the phase-routing steps do not fully encode these parallel streams.

“then poured into a 0.2 M solution of NaOH (30 mL) and Et2O (50 mL)” establishes that the receiving liquids precede transfer of the reaction mixture, but does not specify their relative charging order. workup_receiver is a logical destination label, not an asserted apparatus identity.
